set_aside.subject: record-type taxonomy for listing
set_aside.text: a table keyed by the record type and total over its members
set_aside.question: What closed type defines the members of “record type,” and which module owns that type, so LISTABLE_RECORD_TYPES can be total and shared without inventing a second taxonomy?
options: A `models` enumeration of all record types
A surface-operation-specific record-type enumeration owned by `data_provider`
The set of row-model classes, with an explicitly defined conversion to request values
set_aside.default_guess: Define the closed record-type enumeration in `models` and key LISTABLE_RECORD_TYPES by it.

set_aside.subject: pagination type and filter whitelist used by persistence
set_aside.text: the record types `list_records` lists and the filter fields each may be listed by ... this module holds only the values
set_aside.question: How does `store_persistence`, whose Knows list contains only `models`, obtain the LISTABLE_RECORD_TYPES and PAGE_FILTERS restrictions needed to expose only the stated typed page operations and “nothing else”?
options: The generated StoreRepository port carries the closed allowed operations into `store_persistence`
`store_persistence` exposes a broader typed primitive and `store` or `surface` alone enforces the whitelist
set_aside.default_guess: Have the generated repository port carry the closed allowed operations, while `surface` remains the owner of request refusal.

set_aside.subject: StoreRepository interface
set_aside.text: Every read and write of a row goes through one typed record port, `StoreRepository`: an interface ... Its one implementation is `SqliteStoreRepository`, owned by `store_persistence`
set_aside.question: Which module owns and declares the StoreRepository interface, so `store` can consume it and the earlier `store_persistence` module can implement it without depending upward on `store`?
options: `store_persistence` owns both the interface and implementation
`models` owns the interface as shared typed data
A separate lower-level port module owns the interface
Structural conformance is intended, with no imported interface declaration
set_aside.default_guess: Let `store_persistence` declare the interface beside its implementation and let `store` depend on that interface.

set_aside.subject: spool ceiling enforcement
set_aside.text: `store.spool_file` alone checks both ceilings of A15 rule 3 — the file against `spool_file_bytes_max`, the run's spooled files plus this one against `spool_run_bytes_max` — and on a refusal keeps nothing of that file or of any file the same attempt spooled before it; files of earlier attempts stay. / the two spool ceilings of A20, checked on publishing, and discarding every file of the refused attempt
set_aside.question: Does `store` own and perform the two spool-ceiling checks, or does `store_spool` own and perform them during publication?
options: `store` checks both ceilings and orders discard through `store_spool`
`store_spool` checks both ceilings and reports the refusal through `store`
The check is deliberately split, with an exact division that must be stated
set_aside.default_guess: Treat `store_spool` as the sole checker because it owns ceiling accounting and attempt discard, with `store.spool_file` only exposing that result.

set_aside.subject: SpooledFileKey
set_aside.text: the name of a spooled file inside its run's spool directory, made from its SpooledFileKey
set_aside.question: What are the fields and owner of SpooledFileKey, and does `store` construct and pass it or does `store_spool` construct it from separate typed position facts?
options: A private `store_spool` value built from typed arguments
A store-owned port value passed to `store_spool`
set_aside.default_guess: Make it a private `store_spool` value constructed from typed run, node, map-index, attempt, port and list-index arguments.
